transcript.text: A dishwasher showing 'no power' usually points to a simple electrical issue first. Please check if the appliance is plugged in securely and whether any household fuses or RCDs have tripped. If the power is fine but there are still no lights or sounds when you press the button, it could be a door latch switch or an internal wiring fault.
its a Neff integrated, so no plug to see. nothing tripped at the consumer unit and the other sockets and lights work. still totally dead, no lights at all

Because your Neff is integrated with no visible plug, it will be hard-wired via a switched spur (a small switch on the wall above the worktop). Even if the main consumer unit hasn't tripped, that specific switch could be off or faulty. Please check if that switch is in the 'on' position. If you have another appliance handy, try plugging it into that same socket to confirm there is actually 240V coming through. If the spur has power but the dishwasher remains dead, we will need the model number (usually on a label on the side edge of the door) to check for an internal blown fuse or wiring issue.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
the spur switch above the worktop is on and the neon light is lit. model on the door edge label is S513G60X0G. what next?

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. The most common cause on integrated Neff dishwashers like your S513G60X0G is a blown mains input fuse or a loose connection at the terminal block where the power enters the machine. 1. Turn off the spur switch at the wall and wait 1 minute.
2. Remove the kickplate (usually held by two screws) to access the wiring compartment behind it.
3. Locate the terminal block where the mains wires enter; look for a small glass fuse holder (often white or black).
4. Check if the fuse is seated tightly and if the wire inside looks intact (unbroken). Also check that the main power wires are not loose. If the fuse is blown, it may need replacing, but note that fuses often blow due to a deeper fault in the PCB or heating element. If you are not comfortable doing this, or if the fuse is fine and still no power, please call an engineer as the issue likely lies with the main control board.
I've got no meter or spare fuse and can't pull the dishwasher out, so I'm not sure I can check that. Is there anything else I can try?

Unfortunately, there isn't much more you can try at this stage. Since the spur switch is most likely on and the machine remains totally dead with no lights or sounds, the fault is probably internal—most commonly a blown mains input fuse or a failed control board (PCB).

candidates: Power supply issue (tripped RCD/fuse or loose plug) (high)
Control panel lockout or delayed start feature active (medium)
Internal fault (door switch, wiring loom, or PCB) (low)
plan: The fault they reported is: "won't come on". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the one or two safe checks, or the one question, that would best tell those causes apart. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.

candidates: Isolated switched spur (switch above worktop) is off or faulty (high)
Internal mains fuse or wiring fault at the dishwasher input (medium)
